A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FoD research despite the changed title and narrower scope. All 28 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original restoration experiments, image-to-image translation results, CIFAR-10 generation results, and ablation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original restoration results and reports additional experiments on efficiency, schedules, backbones, sampling steps, and JPEG artifact removal.

M1.justification: The core FoD SDE, residual regression loss, and EM/MC/NMC sampling procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D.4 adds experimental FoD variants with an attention-equipped U-Net and a ViT backbone, extending v2's attention-free U-Net implementation.

E1.justification: The four principal restoration datasets remain unchanged. v3 removes the image-to-image translation tasks and CIFAR-10 unconditional generation evaluation, while adding JPEG artifact removal trained on DIV2K and evaluated on LIVE1. This substantially refocuses coverage on restoration.

E2.justification: UniDB is added to all four principal restoration comparisons, and GOUB joins the qualitative comparisons. Removing the translation and CIFAR-10 evaluations also removes comparisons involving SDEdit, DDPM, Score SDE, NCSN/NCSNv2, and several flow-matching configurations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce schedule and backbone variations, ReFlow evaluations at 10/20/50/100 steps, JPEG quality factor 10, and wall-clock efficiency measurements. The existing U-Net baseline's stated loss changes from L1 to L2 despite unchanged scores; the PDFs do not establish that it was rerun. The principal dataset splits and default FoD training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds schedule sensitivity, backbone ablations, ReFlow step-count sensitivity, GOUB/FoD noise-localization comparisons, and explicit failure-case analysis. JPEG restoration tests behavior beyond localized degradations. v2's noise-ablation learning curves and translation/unconditional variant analyses are removed; its approximation-error table and comprehensive FoD sampler-step plots are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Appendix D.1 newly specifies one stochastic output per test image without averaging multiple draws; v2 leaves this unspecified. This discloses sampling repetition rather than establishing a change in runs. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, or error bars.

E6.justification: The retained principal restoration and MC/NMC scores are unchanged. v3 adds UniDB results, schedule/backbone/ReFlow-step results, JPEG scores, and measured inference times, including 3.85 seconds for 100-step FoD and 0.43 seconds for 10-step MC sampling. The translation and CIFAR-10 result sets are removed.

T1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a finite-time expected-residual bound and log-residual variance derivation, supporting approximate rather than exact endpoint convergence. Appendix A makes schedule assumptions explicit. The main closed-form solution, KL/Taylor derivations, maximum-likelihood discussion, and connections to flow matching and stochastic interpolants are largely retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The paper narrows its central contribution from a general generative framework demonstrated on restoration and translation to efficient image restoration. The abstract replaces the state-of-the-art claim with strong overall performance against representative generative restoration methods and removes the translation applicability claim.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges PMRF's higher inpainting PSNR, qualifies sampler perceptual tradeoffs, and attributes efficiency primarily to fewer sampling steps while recognizing backbone differences. It adds limitations concerning paired degradations, independent perturbations, missing regression baselines, unmeasured variability, and semantic failures. The earlier unconditional-generation limitation is removed with that evaluation.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents batch size 16, paired 256-by-256 training crops, original-resolution evaluation, single-output sampling, metric implementations, and baseline backbone/parameter differences. Translation and CIFAR-10 implementation information is removed. The core training budget, GPU specification, and FoD code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Background and related work are substantially refocused on restoration, diffusion bridges, and FoD's relationship to stochastic interpolants. New references include diffusion bridge matching, Peluchetti's forward-time diffusions, DDBM, and UniDB, while numerous general generation and translation references are removed.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, method exposition, discussion, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around restoration. Variational material and connections to prior work move into reorganized appendices; sampling gains a dedicated subsection, and a broader-impact statement is added.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is rebuilt around an IR-SDE/FoD comparison, and the four-panel benchmark table becomes two tables with method categories. Sampling and ablation tables are reformatted, sampler plots move into the main text, and new analysis displays are added. Translation/CIFAR-10 galleries and noise-ablation learning curves disappear, alongside a document-wide journal-layout change.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the support and calibration of the restoration contribution. Actual timings and backbone disclosures substantiate efficiency beyond step counts, while new sensitivity checks and failure analyses address previously untested explanations and boundaries. Performance and finite-time convergence claims better match the evidence. Translation and CIFAR-10 evidence is lost as the scope explicitly narrows, and uncertainty estimates remain absent, but the targeted validation and more accurate qualifications provide a clear overall quality gain.
